sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 4

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 4:1
items.html:
It explains the ten Sefirot that emerge one above the other, and it contains two matters: 1. That all the 100 Sefirot that emerge in a coupling by striking at an equal level are counted as only a single Sefira. 2. The ten Sefirot whose level is equal emerge from a single coupling by striking, whereas the ten Sefirot that emerge one above the other emerge from five couplings by striking.

From the five phases of coarseness, five levels of ten Sefirot emerge one above the other by way of refinement
Now we shall explain the ten Sefirot that emerge one above the other. And know that, on account of the five phases in the vessel of Malchut of which we have spoken, there came out for us five phases of levels that emerge by the aforementioned coupling by striking, one above the other, on account of the refining of the screen and its passing through the five phases of coarseness of which we have spoken in the vessel of Malchut. For when the screen is upon the full coarseness in the vessel of Malchut, which is called the coarseness of phase four, it is discerned that there are five phases in the reflected light that is rejected from her, and therefore they clothe all five phases of direct light. However, if the coarseness of phase four was refined, it turns out that the reflected light that is rejected from her falls short of clothing the phase of Keter of direct light, for there are in it only four phases. And this matter has already been explained at sufficient length in Inner Observation (Part 2, Item 72, Sub Header, “And in order”), and you shall seek it out from there; there is no need to expand upon it here.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 4:2
items.html: However, we must know that in every expansion of upper light for a coupling by striking, according to the order of degrees of the five phases of coarseness in the aforementioned screen — although there are in each expansion 100 Sefirot, which are ten Sefirot of length and ten Sefirot of thickness, as above — they are nevertheless counted as only a single Sefira, that is, only after the name of the uppermost Sefira in it. If the upper one is Keter, they are all called Keter; and if its level is the Sefira of Hochma, they are all called Hochma, and so forth in this manner.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 4:3
items.html: Thus these five levels that emerge on account of the refining of the screen, one above the other, from the level of Keter to the level of Malchut, are counted as only five Sefirot: KHB TM. And although in each level of them there are ten Sefirot in length and ten Sefirot in thickness, nevertheless, since all these 100 Sefirot are found at an equal level, they are for this reason counted as only a single Sefira, which is named after the uppermost one, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 4:4
items.html: And you see the great difference between ten Sefirot whose level is equal and ten Sefirot that stand one above the other. For the ten Sefirot whose level is equal emerge from a single coupling by striking, and they are all counted as a single Sefira. The ten Sefirot KHB TM that emerge one above the other, however, emerge by way of five couplings by striking, on account of the refining of the screen in the order of the degrees, from phase four to phase three, and so on, up to the root; and in each one of them there are ten Sefirot in length and ten Sefirot in thickness, at an equal level. Therefore these five levels are counted as only KHB TM, one above the other — that is, after the name of the upper Sefirot in these five levels. And so the great difference between the five kinds of ten Sefirot has been explained, namely: ten Sefirot of direct light, when they are by themselves; ten Sefirot of direct light and reflected light, whose level is equal; ten Sefirot of Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya and Yechida; ten Sefirot of root, Neshama, Guf, garment and hall; and ten Sefirot that stand one above the other.
